alignments.note: The fronted question auxiliary Shall belongs to the interrogative particle (rule 17).
Qal passive rendered be taken; discontinuous around the fronted subject noun (rule 25), headed on the lexical verb.
Preposition and its own suffix fused into thereof, one unit under rules 22 and 30, headed on the preposition.
Subject noun of the passive clause.
Purpose לְ before an infinitive, rendered to.
The ASV promotes the phrase to the bare object of make and writes no word for this לְ (rule 40).

The supplied determiner any belongs to the nominal expression it determines, as rule 15 gives an indefinite article to its noun; the competing reading marks any added under rule 30, since no כֹּל stands here as it does at s019.

אִם opening the second, disjunctive question takes the connective or and the fronted auxiliary will (rules 14 and 17); headed on or as the word carrying its lexeme. The competing reading leaves will with the imperfect verb.
Finite verb, discontinuous from its auxiliary and separated from it by the added subject noun (rule 25).
Here the ASV writes two English words, of it, so rule 30's one-word condition is unmet and the preposition takes only of, unlike the fused thereof above.
Noun with the English indefinite article, which belongs to the noun (rule 15).
Preposition and suffix fused into thereon (rules 22, 30), headed on the preposition.
Supplied lexical subject noun where no source nominal stands, exactly as rule 17's יָשְׁבוּ בָהּ → men shall dwell therein leaves men added.

review_notes: The verse writes the same מִן + suffix twice and the ASV renders it once as thereof and once as of it; the fusion condition of rule 30 is met only in the first, so the two are aligned differently.
any before work is given to the noun as a supplied determiner; the alternative added reading is recorded in that unit's note.
